prompts: A client loves the woodblock print attached, also in {WS}/print.jpg; it is in the public domain. They want a 3D wallpaper that copies it: its composition, its palette and its subjects, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it at a glance, rebuilt as our own low poly scene with some gentle motion. Deliver {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code: the print is the reference, not a texture. Record in {WS}/result.json what you took from it: boats (how many the print shows) and mountain (its name). It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal] Rebuild the attached woodblock print as a single-file 3D low-poly wallpaper, recording what was taken from it.

[action] Read ./print.jpg visually, wrote ./result.json, then built ./scene/index.html: one file, all geometry in code (Three.js 0.170.0 from the allowed jsdelivr CDN, Zen Old Mincho from Google Fonts, no texture from the print). Scene: claw-crested breaking wave left, second wave right, three tan boats with crews bobbing on an animated swell field, small snow-capped Fuji on a grey horizon band under paper-cream sky, foam-blob jitter, vertical title cartouche and red seal. Verified by opening the file in a browser and screenshotting three times; fixed dark "cliff" waves (fill light, orientation), rock-like foam (smaller cream blobs), and wave scale/position. My tab was closed after review.

[result] ./scene/index.html renders the print's composition, palette and subjects with gentle motion, no build step; ./result.json records boats: 3, mountain: "Mount Fuji", plus the exact palette and composition notes.

[findings and evidence] The print is Hokusai's "The Great Wave off Kanagawa" (神奈川沖浪裏, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji): its cartouche reads 冨嶽三十六景 / 神奈川沖浪裏, and the image shows exactly three boats (one caught in the wave at left, one climbing the right swell, one foreground) and a tiny snow-capped Mount Fuji on the horizon. I know it is right because I read the image directly (cartouche text and boat count visible) and confirmed the delivered scene live: the last browser screenshot shows the recognizable wave-boats-Fuji layout in the print's blue/cream palette before I closed the tab.

[assumptions] Wallpaper is full-viewport with no UI controls; motion kept subtle (swell, bobbing boats, quivering foam); boats are the passenger/cargo oshiokuri type the print shows; camera framing approximates the print's aspect.
